## Authentication and restricted peers

The related-seats route is registered inside the bearer middleware. Authentication and peer restrictions run before dispatch; invalid credentials receive 401 (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:739,812-857). Local machine and paired-peer credentials produce distinct identities, and duplicate local/peer keys are rejected by configuration (crates/daemon/src/http/auth.rs:109-118,129-145).

GET /v1/seats/related is not in the restricted-peer allowlist: it resolves to PeerAccess::Refused. Adding scope=local cannot change that because the query is consulted only for LocalScopeOnly, while Refused always denies (http/mod.rs:487-542). The check uses Axum's matched route template, sharing route identity with dispatch rather than comparing independent raw-path prefixes. Peers retain GET /v1/seats?scope=local for seat reads; this change does not grant them closed-row enumeration.

## Enumeration and query safety

Local machine bearer holders may query another closed local seat's descriptor. Selectors match id OR native session OR PID and include tombstones; they are not caller-seat ownership proofs (http/mod.rs:4479-4517; crates/store/src/registry.rs:473-498). This is intentional machine-level read authority, classified in harness/scripts/route-inventory.json:219-229. C33's same-user trust boundary does not extend to paired peers.

The registry SQL is static and selectors are bound parameters, not interpolated SQL or wildcard matching (registry.rs:476-493). The changed status selection also uses bound parameters (crates/store/src/status.rs:30,128-154). The extension builds query parameters with URLSearchParams (.copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:389-395). The handler requires at least one optional SeatId/session/u32-PID selector; it has no explicit id/session length or canonical-format restriction, and empty strings count as present. No exploitable introduced issue was identified from those facts. Global URI limits and malformed-input behavior were not probed.

## Privacy and resource shape

All 14 changed-file deltas were reviewed. No identified real credentials, private transcript content, private repository identities, or prohibited machine-specific paths were added. Fixture credentials are dummy values. No dependency manifests or lockfiles changed.

One related-row HTTP request replaces the full roster request in the existing registration loop; no new timer or process-launch site was introduced. Existing backoff starts at 250 ms and doubles to 5 seconds (.copilot/extensions/pij/extension.mjs:221-303). Qualifying closed-own-id registrations stop terminally; absent prebind rows and old-daemon 404s remain retryable (store.mjs:488-498,827-833). The packet's CPU timings, live-seat comparison and post-bounce savings were not independently measured; the performance role owns that proof.
